I am 59, been farming this land in Quzhou for 30 years now. My main rotation is wheat-maize on most of the land, and I keep a small piece for cotton because the price has been decent and I know how to grow it. Total 13.1 mu — I will put about 5 mu in cotton this year, and the other 8 mu stays in the wheat-maize double crop like always.

Let me think this through. Last year wheat gave me around 480-500 kg per mu, maize around 580 kg. That is normal for our area. Soil here in Quzhou is alluvial, decent but salty in patches, and we have been double-cropping for years so organic matter is not great. I read the soil test results from the village last year — phosphorus is medium, potassium is okay, nitrogen is what I need to watch.

For wheat I already planted in October — I used Jimai 22, an improved variety, 15 kg seed per mu, and put down compound fertilizer 15-15-15 at planting, about 50 kg. Now in spring I need to topdress urea around jointing, maybe 20-25 kg per mu. Total nitrogen pure for the season comes to about 18 kg N per mu. I will irrigate at jointing and again at grain filling — two times if rain is short. Spray once for aphids and powdery mildew, maybe twice if the weather turns warm and wet.

For maize after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, hybrid seed, no tillage, just stubble retention. Base fertilizer compound 20 kg, then topdress urea 25 kg at big trumpet stage. That gives me about 16 kg N per mu. One irrigation at tasseling if dry. Spray for armyworm and corn borer once or twice.

Cotton is more work. I plant Lumianyan or a Bt variety to save on bollworm spray. Plough the cotton ground because it needs deeper soil. Apply more potassium for cotton — it is hungry for K. About 12 kg N, 6 kg P, 10 kg K per mu, base plus topdress at flowering. Irrigate 3-4 times. Spray 4-5 times — aphids, mites, bollworm even with Bt because of secondary pests.
